Article Title: Over 3 lakh Punjab govt employees continue mass leave on day-3 as talks fail; bus staff extend strike indefinitely
Article Text:
Bus staff protest in Patiala on Wednesday





CHANDIGARH: Over three lakh Punjab govt employees took mass casual leave on Wednesday over pending demands, disrupting work across govt offices. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services.Employee representatives met chief secretary KAP Sinha at 4 pm after the govt released minutes of an earlier meeting with chief minister Bhagwant Mann, as demanded by unions. However, the nearly two-hour meeting remained inconclusive.Sukhchain Singh Khaira, coordinator of the Joint Action Committee leading the agitation, said work across govt offices, including directorates, was affected. Sahil Sharma, general secretary of the Punjab Civil Secretariat Employees Union, alleged the govt was delaying a resolution by asking unions to reiterate demands already raised in previous meetings.A 39-member delegation of employees and pensioners later met officials but said it received no clear assurances on several demands. They said the govt had clarified that temporary teachers described as regularised had only been given “security of tenure”, without the financial benefits available to regular employees.The delegation also said the govt had no roadmap for Anganwadi, ASHA and mid-day meal workers.The future course of the agitation will be decided at a meeting in Ludhiana on Oct 25. Employees are demanding release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of contractual staff, revision of pensions, restoration of 37 discontinued allowances and the cashless health scheme. They have also sought withdrawal of notifications imposing central pay scales and a three-year probation period.The standoff continues despite a Sept 18 meeting between Mann and employee and pensioner representatives, when the chief minister announced an 8% DA hike in two instalments of 4% each from Oct 1 and promised regular monthly meetings.Meanwhile, transport workers extended their strike after talks with a cabinet minister failed to resolve demands for regularisation under service rules, direct departmental contracts for outsourced workers and withdrawal of police cases linked to earlier protests.Union general secretary Shamsher Singh said proposals covering around 1,400 outsourced Punjab Roadways employees and more than 1,700 PRTC workers remained pending. A Sept 21 govt letter had set a one-month deadline to shift workers from outsourcing agencies to direct contracts, but it passed without implementation, he said. A proposal to withdraw cases had also been sent to the Punjab DGP, but no further action had followed despite workers securing bail.The union plans a joint demonstration with Theka Mulazam Sangharsh Morcha in Dirba, the constituency of transport and finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema. Workers from all 27 depots and two sub-depots plan to assemble in Mohali and march towards Punjab Vidhan Sabha and the chief minister’s official residence.Union representatives alleged that shortages of spare parts and tyres had grounded several buses and criticised PRTC management for issuing show-cause notices and termination warnings. However, PRTC GM Operations A S Tiwana said more than 800 of the corporation’s 1,250 buses operated on Wednesday. He said management had proposed bringing around 1,719 outsourced employees under contractual terms.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh called the mass leave a sign of a deepening crisis of confidence between the Mann govt and its employees. He demanded immediate talks and time-bound solutions, accusing the govt of prioritising publicity over public grievances.
Article Summary: Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday.

Article Title: Mettur Dam water release for Cauvery delta irrigation to end tonight after 45 days
Article Text:
The Mettur Dam





SALEM: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night, as the 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from catchment areas in Karnataka. The water level stood at about 91.56 feet against the dam’s full capacity of 120 feet when releases began. The schedule was intended to support irrigation across the Cauvery delta region.On Thursday morning, the reservoir level stood at 59.13 feet, down from about 91.56 feet on September 1. Storage was recorded at 24.04 tmc ft, while inflow had fallen to 696 cusecs.Water Resources Department (WRD) officials said the dam’s storage levels and future inflows would determine any further decisions on irrigation releases.
Article Summary: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night. The 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from Karnataka.

Article Title: 7 years apart, anti-drug activist Parvinder Jhota’s killing revives memories of Neha Shoree murder
Article Text:
Neha Shoree, Parvinder Jhota (File Photos)

Neha Shoree: A licence cancelled and then a killing

Parvinder Singh Jhota: The 2023 dispute that preceded his killing

A continuing challenge for Punjab





CHANDIGARH: Seven years after Punjab drug licensing officer Neha Shoree was shot dead in her office, the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa has brought renewed attention to the risks faced by those who challenge alleged illegal drug sales in the state.The two cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons. But both brought allegations of illegal drug sales into focus and raised questions about the enforcement of laws governing medicines and addictive substances.Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Jhota, 45, was shot dead in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs.Four other people were injured in the firing, which was captured during Jhota’s Facebook Live broadcast.Shoree was selected as a drug inspector through the Punjab Public Service Commission in 2007 and joined the health department in Ropar that October. In 2013, she was given the responsibility of district zonal licensing authority.On March 29, 2019, she was shot dead at her office by Balwinder Singh, a chemist from Morinda whose shop licence she had cancelled in 2009, police said.During her tenure as a drug inspector in Ropar, Shoree had raided shops and seized banned drugs.Her parents alleged that the drug mafia was behind the killing because she had exposed the sale of intoxicants in the Ropar and Kharar region.“We want to question Prime Minister Narendra Modi that you have been assuring to make a drug-free country but here women officers are being killed by drug mafia,” her mother and paternal aunt said, according to a TOI report published on March 31, 2019.The family’s allegations prompted demands for a wider investigation. The then Punjab chief minister, Capt Amarinder Singh, subsequently handed the probe to ADGP Prabodh Kumar, director of the Bureau of Investigation.However, in December 2019, police informed the Punjab and Haryana high court that their investigation had found no involvement of the drug mafia or any other person besides the accused.Shoree’s family continued to question the findings and seek further investigation.In September 2019, the Punjab government approved financial benefits of around Rs 31 lakh for her family. Shoree’s killing had also prompted scrutiny of the licensing process and the circumstances surrounding the accused’s arms licence.Jhota became known in Mansa for confronting medical store owners whom he accused of selling intoxicating pills, synthetic drugs and other prohibited substances. He recorded confrontations and shared videos on social media.His dispute with medical store owner Ashwani Kumar dated back to July 2023. Jhota had allegedly put a garland of shoes around Kumar’s neck in a public confrontation, accusing him of selling synthetic drugs.A case was registered against Jhota, who was arrested and spent nearly two months in jail. He was released on September 11, 2023, after the complainant approached the court to withdraw the complaint.The case against Kumar concerning the alleged sale of prohibited substances remained pending.Jhota continued his campaign. On the morning of October 13, 2026, he reportedly met an elderly man who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store and took him to Kumar’s shop to question the owner about the alleged sale.The confrontation escalated as Jhota livestreamed it on Facebook. Kumar allegedly pulled out a firearm and opened fire inside the shop before following the injured activist into the street and firing again. Jhota was hit by three bullets and died at Mansa Civil Hospital. Four others were also injured.In the video, Jhota is heard saying, “maar mainu, maar mainu” (kill me).Kumar fled after the shooting and was arrested in Rajasthan’s Salasar on October 14. Police also detained an alleged associate accused of helping him escape.Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, a retired Army serviceman, refused to cremate his son until those responsible were brought to justice.“I am still alive and pledge to fight against the drug peddlers as my son was waging a war against them. I am also ready to take a bullet if the peddlers are not taken to task,” Bhim Singh said at Mansa Civil Hospital.The killings have brought renewed attention to the state’s efforts to curb drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of addictive pharmaceutical substances. Following Jhota’s murder, the Punjab government stepped up inspections of chemist shops.The two cases must be viewed in their individual contexts: Shoree was a government officer carrying out licensing duties, while Jhota was an activist who publicly confronted people he accused of selling prohibited substances.Investigators in Shoree’s case said they found no evidence of anyone else being involved in her murder, while the investigation into Jhota’s killing concerns a separate accused and a separate dispute.Their deaths, years apart, have nevertheless renewed questions about the availability of addictive substances, the enforcement of drug-sale regulations and the safety of people who seek to expose alleged violations.
Article Summary: Neha Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Parvinder Singh Jhota, 45, was killed in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs. Both cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons.

Article Title: ‘Don’t trouble me, I’ll commit suicide’: Absconding in Shiva Sharma death case, model Shraddha Dubey releases another video
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey, accused of killing her businessman boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, has released another.

The 1st video





LUCKNOW: Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, has released another video on Thursday claiming that the two had been dating for the past two months and that Sharma was under a massive debt.In the five-minute-long video, Dubey recounted the events leading up to Sharma’s death.Dubey alleged that Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans.She said she could show screenshots to support her claims.In the video, Dubey also appealed to people to stop harassing her, warning that she would die by suicide if the alleged torture continued.“Think why would someone kill someone and throw them from their own apartment,” she said, questioning the allegations against her.She urged the media not to spread rumours without evidence. Referring to Sharma’s mother, Dubey alleged that she had started a quarrel with her driver in the hospital. She then said, “It's not like you have lost a son, I have lost my boyfriend.”Dubey claimed that she and Sharma had not spoken to each other for six to seven days before the incident.On October 7, Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor and was crying, she said."Then I called him twice from my number. He did not pick up the call at that time. Later, he called me around 2am. I asked him what happened to which he asked me to meet him. We met, went to cafe where he ordered coffee for me and juice for himself," she said, adding that he had a "lot of beers" before meeting her."Later, both of us went to my place. While he drove my car, my driver took his car," she said.Dubey said her sister, Rashmi, visited her home on October 8 to discuss a puja for Navratri. She denied her sister's involvement in the case, claiming that Rashmi barely knew Sharma and had hardly spoken to him."My sister has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva that well. She never spoke to him...My sister and I, we went for a walk that evening. Shiva's friends joined us - one of them was Ashwini Mishra and other named Harsh. We all went for a long drive. I spoke to Shiva, his mother, brother-in-law, and sister too that day," she said.Recounting the day Sharma died, Dubey claimed that he appeared depressed on October 9. She said they woke up and made tea before he went to the washroom."I don't even know what it was. We woke up, made tea. Shiva went to the washroom. Usually, he would never close the main gate. But this time, he did. I asked my sister to go check up on him after a while. As soon as she opened the gate, he jumped from the balcony," she said.Dubey alleged that Sharma's mother accused them of murder and assaulted her driver when she arrived at the hospital."It will be recorded on the hospital's camera. Without knowing anything, she accused us of murder. Without thinking, she blamed us for murder. She blamed us so badly that we might not be able to get out of that blame for life," she said.Earlier, Dubey had released another video denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials, saying she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she had said.Dubey had also denied being absconding and claimed she wanted to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said in the earlier video.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following his death, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim investigators are examining.Lucknow Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey claims her boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, was under a massive debt. Dubey says Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans. Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of his apartment in Lucknow.

Article Title: After Google renames 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US; CEO Sundar Pichai says no to US government's request on changing name of Atlantic Ocean; tells: No, no, no, this time I'm not doing it
Article Text:
Trump said he called Google to rename 'Atlantic Ocean' to 'Trump Ocean'

Trump wants to rename ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’

US previously renamed Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario

President Trump, who floated the idea of renaming ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’ earlier this month, has once again raised the possibility of renaming the ocean. Speaking at an event recently, Trump revealed that he called Google Maps and asked to rename the Atlantic Ocean. He said that Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to his proposal saying: “No, no, no. This time I'm not doing it.” According to Trump, Pichai said, “Oceans are different, sir. They cover a lot of countries. Please don't ask us to do that.” This comes months after Google renamed 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US following an executive order signed by Trump.As mentioned above, Trump first discussed renaming the Atlantic Ocean this month. “We’ve got the gulf. We’ve got a beautiful lake,” Trump said during a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee. “Now, somebody said, you need a river. We need a river. We need an ocean.”He jokingly said that the new name could be in honor of him. “We call it ‘Trump Ocean’ or ‘Ocean of the Americas,’ something like that,” Trump said further adding “Before I get out, I think we should have an ocean. And we need a great river.”Earlier this month, the US administration renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, sparking diplomatic tensions between the US and Mexico.In August, Trump also renamed Lake Ontario, between New York and Canada, as “Lake America”.After an executive order, Google posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses. Apple followed the suit renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America on Maps for US users.
Article Summary: Trump said he called Google to rename 'Atlantic Ocean' to 'Trump Ocean' He said that Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to his proposal saying: “No, no, no. This time I'm not doing it.” This comes months after Google renamed Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' in the US following an executive order signed by Trump.

Article Title: Bhopal newspaper hawker arranging papers on his scooter at 5am suffers severe leg injury after speeding SUV rams parked sedan, pushing it into his scooter; CCTV captures driver and woman passenger fle
Article Text:
A 36-year-old newspaper hawker named Rajkumar Malviya was badly injured after a crash





BHOPAL: A 36-year-old newspaper hawker suffered a severe injury in his left leg after a speeding SUV rammed into a parked sedan, pushing it into his scooter while he was arranging newspapers in DK-2 Danish Kunj under Kolar police station limits around 5am on Thursday. The collision also damaged another scooter parked alongside his vehicle.The incident was captured on CCTV footage from a shop opposite the accident spot. The footage reportedly shows the SUV driver and a woman passenger getting out of the vehicle and leaving the scene after the crash.According to the complaint, the driver abandoned the black SUV and fled. The injured hawker also alleged that the driver was under the influence of alcohol.The complainant, Rajkumar Malviya, a resident of Baba Nagar in Shahpura, told police that he reaches Danish Kunj around 4.30am daily to collect newspapers of different publications for distribution.Around 5am on Thursday, he was loading newspapers onto his scooter when the SUV approached from the Jain temple side at high speed and allegedly rammed into a parked sedan. The impact pushed the sedan backwards into Malviya’s scooter and another two-wheeler parked beside it, damaging both and injuring his left knee badly.Malviya’s colleague, Gaman, took him to a private hospital, where he was undergoing treatment when police recorded his statement in the emergency ward around 9am.Kolar police registered a case under the BNS for rash and negligent driving and an act endangering life and public safety. Police are investigating the crash and the allegations against the driver.
Article Summary: A 36-year-old newspaper hawker suffered a severe injury in his left leg after a speeding SUV rammed into a parked sedan. The collision also damaged another scooter parked alongside his vehicle. The incident was captured on CCTV footage from a shop opposite the accident spot. According to the complaint, the driver abandoned the black SUV and fled.

Article Title: 'Am studying his body': Trump goes into graphic detail about US senator's body at rally
Article Text:
Trump describes Senator Jon Husted’s physique in graphic detail at a North Carolina rally, calling him “a pile of muscle” and “a monster”

US President Donald Trump went into graphic detail about Republican Senator Jon Husted’s physique during a campaign rally in Greenville, North Carolina, continuing his unusual praise of the Ohio senator’s muscular build."I'm studying his body. I've never studied the body of a man before. It's not my thing. Nothing wrong with it, of course. But it's never been my thing," Trump told the audience.He then described Husted’s physique, saying, "But I looked at his a**. I said, 'His a**, s***, it's like a pile of muscle.' Then I looked at his legs and I said, 'Man, his feet are big.'"Trump also described Husted as being built like "a piece of steel" and called him "a monster".The remarks came as Trump campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley in North Carolina on Tuesday.Despite campaigning for a candidate in another state, Trump returned to talking about Husted, whom he had similarly praised at a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, last week.Husted, who became a US senator in January 2025 after a special election to replace JD Vance, previously served as Ohio's lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025. He is facing Democratic challenger Sherrod Brown in the November midterm elections.Trump has been campaigning across Republican-leaning states, urging voters to support candidates he has endorsed ahead of the midterm polls.

Article Title: Beginning in 1925, Minnesota farmer John Christensen spent more than a decade transforming a cellar project into a 14,000-square-foot rock garden of castles, bridges and ponds
Article Text:
AI Representation: Minnesota farmer John Christensen began building the 14,000-square-foot Itasca Rock Garden in 1925. Image credits: Chatgpt

A retired farmer and a 1925 excavation near Albert Lea

A castle, ponds and bridges across 14,000 square feet

John Christensen’s

Itasca Rock Garden

Albert Lea, Minnesota, lies in Freeborn County’s glacial farmland, where John L. Christensen began building Itasca Rock Garden in 1925. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Rocks and geodes gathered on trips

The last work in 1938

Johnson family care from 1954 to 1985

A Kohler restoration was completed in 2022

Albert Lea is a city in Freeborn County in southern Minnesota, an area of farmland where glaciers left behind stones of many sizes and colors. This meant clearing away all the rocks on the farms yearly, which was an undertaking for the farmers. In one case in the Albert Lea community, a farmer found a different use for all these rocks. John Christensen lived outside town with his wife, Sophie. After he stopped farming, he began digging at his home and the site grew into a landscape of castles, ponds and bridges.Christensen had been farming in Minnesota for 40 years when he cleared many glacial boulders from his land, Raw Vision states and only after retirement did he realize their beauty and usefulness. In 1925, the magazine adds, he began excavating a basement for a vegetable cellar beneath their house. The SPACES Archives entry Itasca Rock Garden (Christensen Rock Garden) tells it differently. Christensen first set out to build the largest structure on the property, a rock and concrete castle big enough for several standing adults, to serve as a root and vegetable cellar.The Kohler Foundation page onstates that Christensen built a 14,000-square-foot rock garden of castles, ponds, bridges and grottos over a decade or so beginning in 1925. According to Raw Vision, the huge castle had turrets on top of it and 1925 written on its stone structure. Walkways with steps and archways ran around the ponds, while waterfalls, benches and a small castle birdhouse rounded off the project.Roadside America points out that the ponds once held fish and working fountains and Raw Vision adds that lily pads floated in them. The SPACES website describes the same landscape, with rock walls, miniatures, a circular seating area and a second, smaller castle.The Minnesota Museum of the Mississippi’s Itasca Rock Garden entry states that John Christensen and his wife often collected rocks while traveling, bringing home geodes and unusual specimens to incorporate into the garden and a second page from the same museum, titled Christiansen’s Rock Garden after an alternate spelling of the surname, repeats that detail. Sophie planted the flowerbeds and terraces, Raw Vision adds and her plantings added to the garden’s lush, storybook character.The Minnesota Museum of the Mississippi dates the most recent construction in the garden to 1938 and Christensen died in 1939. The SPACES article lists his name and the year 1939 among the garden’s decorations, a date later than the last recorded construction and the article does not say who added it. The museum goes on to state that his widow and later owners continued to maintain the garden and kept it open to the public and a postcard from 1952 shows it in use as a tourist site.Kohler Foundation says that the land was owned by the Johnson family from 1954 to 1985. After the Johnson family’s ownership ended in 1985, the site declined and was eventually foreclosed. Kohler discovered the garden in fall 2019 through descendants of the Johnson family. At the time, the foundation said that the garden was overgrown but the structure could still be seen and that the house was structurally sound.Kohler’s project was finished by 2022. Further gardening followed, including some planting in 2023 and guided tours resumed in 2024. As noted on the Roadside America website, the foundation donated the site to the Freeborn County Historical Society. An appointment is necessary for visiting; the admission fee is quoted at $5 for adults, though one should call to make sure. A Raw Vision article written in summer 2024 describes the restored garden as enchanting its keepers and visitors again almost a century after the first stone was laid, which fits the 99 years between 1925 and 2024.
Article Summary: Minnesota farmer John Christensen began building the 14,000-square-foot Itasca Rock Garden in 1925. Christensen first set out to build the largest structure on the property, a rock and concrete castle big enough for several standing adults, to serve as a root and vegetable cellar. Walkways with steps and archways ran around the ponds, while waterfalls, benches and a small castle birdhouse rounded off the project.

Article Title: 'Take it or leave it': Delhi delivery executive's final video recounts torn Rs 10 note row, assault before suicide
Article Text:
Sameer Hussain, a 24-year-old delivery executive, died after being assaulted over a torn Rs 10 note





NEW DELHI: A 24-year-old delivery executive died on October 20, more than two weeks after he was allegedly slapped following a dispute over a torn Rs 10 note in east Delhi's East Vinod Nagar. Police have arrested two men in connection with the case.Sameer Hussain had called the police control room (PCR) at around 11.03pm on October 4, alleging that two residents had assaulted him after he refused to accept a torn currency note as payment for a delivery.In a video recorded during the investigation, Sameer recounted his version of the incident, saying he had gone to deliver coffee to an elderly customer who took around 10-15 minutes to arrange the payment.The customer eventually handed him cash that included a torn Rs 10 note. When Sameer objected, the customer allegedly told him to "take it or leave it".Sameer said he offered to cancel the order and questioned why it had been placed if the payment could not be made properly. He alleged that the customer abused him before another man arrived and slapped him multiple times. The man also allegedly mocked Sameer over his middle-class background.Police later received information that Sameer had allegedly consumed a poisonous substance. He was admitted to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital on October 5 and died on October 20.A medico-legal case was prepared shortly after midnight on October 5, and an FIR was registered at Kalyanpuri police station the same day.Following Sameer's death, police added Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with abetment of suicide, to the case.The two arrested men have been identified as Rakesh alias Bunti (30) and Rampal Singh (65).
Article Summary: Sameer Hussain, a 24-year-old delivery executive, died after being assaulted over a torn Rs 10 note. Police have arrested two men in connection with the case in east Delhi's East Vinod Nagar. Sameer was admitted to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital and died on October 20.

Article Title: Water supply hit in NDMC areas till Nov 8
Article Text: New Delhi: Water supply in New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) areas will be affected till Nov 8 due to the scheduled annual maintenance and repair works at Upper Ganga Canal.An NDMC official informed that water supply from Sonia Vihar WTP has been shut down until midnight of Nov 8 and thus the overall supply will be affected in the NDMC area.“During this closure period, water will be supplied from the Yamuna River . Consequently, the taste of the supplied water may vary. Additionally, a reduction in water supply is expected in the affected areas and may continue in this period,” said the official.Affected areas would be Bharti Nagar, Golf Links, Lodhi Estate, Khan Market, Rabindra Nagar, Parts of Lodhi Road, High Court, Bapa Nagar, Parts of Pandara Rd and Pandara Park, Jor Bagh, Parts of Lodhi Colony, BK Dutt Colony, Amrita Shergil Marg, Parts of Janpath, Aliganj, Parts of Prithviraj Road, Kidwai Nagar and Laxmibai Nagar. President’s Estate, New PMO, Kaka Nagar, JJ camp Safdarjung flyover, JJ camp Delhi flying club will be other affected areas.“For further information regarding the operation of booster pumps and water services, people can contact on numbers provided on website,” said the official.
Article Summary: Water supply in New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) areas will be affected till Nov 8 due to the scheduled annual maintenance and repair works at Upper Ganga Canal. Water supply from Sonia Vihar WTP has been shut down until midnight of Nov 8. A reduction in water supply is expected in the affected areas.

Article Title: Delhi Waqf Board seeks protection of Race Course mosque after utilities disconnected
Article Text:
Delhi Waqf Board has requested protection for the Race Course mosque after its utilities were disconnected (Representative image)

TOI





NEW DELHI: Delhi Waqf Board has sought protection of the nearly 300-year-old Race Course mosque after its electricity and water connections were allegedly disconnected during a demolition drive on Oct 7.In a letter to the authorities on Oct 19, the board’s CEO, Tanvir Ahmad, said, “The mosque and the adjoining qabristan, spread over two bighas, were notified waqf properties under a Delhi administration gazette notification dated Sept 8, 1977. The mosque is under the direct management and control of Delhi Waqf Board, with an imam appointed by the board conducting five daily prayers.”The letter, marked to the ministries of minority affairs and home affairs, and divisional commissioner and DM of New Delhi district, stated the electricity and water links were snapped during removal of jhuggis without any prior notice or apparent valid reason.“This was despite the mosque having a lawful electricity connection since 1976,” it said, noting the mosque is included in NDMC’s heritage list at No. 22 and registered on UMEED portal.The letter alleges that some persons identifying themselves as officers of Land and Development Office (L&DO) visited the mosque on Oct 17 and directed the imam to vacate the premises within three days, stating the mosque would subsequently be removed.Seeking urgent intervention, the board asked the authorities to examine the matter on priority and restore the electricity and water supply.Sources in the ministry of housing and urban affairs stated that L&DO had not issued any notice to the mosque. NDMC did not respond to questions regarding the discontinuation of power and water connections.Ahmad also confirmed that no demolition order had been served. However, Maulana MM Haroon Rahi from the mosque said people were not being allowed to enter the area to offer prayers.During a visit Wednesday,found entry place restricted, with police personnel deployed in and around the site. Debris and ruins of demolished jhuggis were visible near the closed gate. The 53.2 acres of land belongs to L&DO and was handed over to CPWD for maintenance and development.“People, including those coming to offer prayers, were restricted from entering the place to stop encroachers coming again. The demolition happened a few days ago and debris is yet to be removed,” a source said.On the water and power supply being cut off, he said the connections were in the name of imam, not the waqf board.In Oct 2025, a notice was issued to occupants of Bhai Ram Camp, Masjid Camp and DID Camp slum clusters in Race Course Road area, directing them to vacate govt land and relocate to Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board’s (DUSIB) colony in Savda Ghevra within 15 days. Referring to a joint survey conducted by L&DO and DDA in Jan 2024 for the rehabilitation of JJ clusters, it said, “Although the occupants are considered unauthorised occupants of govt land, those found eligible under DUSIB policy have been identified for relocation. ”
Article Summary: Delhi Waqf Board has sought protection of the nearly 300-year-old Race Course mosque. Its electricity and water connections were allegedly disconnected during a demolition drive on Oct 7. The mosque is under the direct management and control of the board.

Article Title: Blue glow in Maharashtra's Arnala sea sparks speculation of bioluminescence
Article Text:
Residents and visitors near Arnala beach in Virar have observed a mysterious blue glow in the sea.





VIRAR: A mysterious blue glow resembling fireflies has been spotted in the sea off Arnala in Virar, leaving residents and visitors amazed. The sight of the water glowing in the dark surprised many, while several fishermen and locals ventured into the sea to enjoy a swim.The unusual phenomenon is suspected to be caused by bioluminescence, a natural process in which certain marine microorganisms emit light. Some types of microscopic plankton produce a bluish glow when disturbed by water movement, making waves and ripples appear to sparkle in the dark.However, the exact cause of the glow observed off Arnala beach has not yet been scientifically established. There is no official confirmation that the phenomenon is a result of bioluminescence, and further verification is needed to determine whether another factor could be responsible.
Article Summary: Mysterious blue glow spotted in the sea off Arnala in Virar. Phenomenon suspected to be caused by bioluminescence. Some microscopic plankton produce a bluish glow when disturbed by water movement, making waves and ripples appear to sparkle in the dark.
